26 For a progressive transverse wave, what describes the term diffraction?
A
the change in observed frequency of a wave due to a movement of the wave source
B
the spreading of a wave as it passes through a gap or around an obstacle
C
when oscillations of a wave are confined to one plane
D
the resultant displacement of two waves is equal to the sum of the displacements of the
individual waves when the waves meet

hints: Notice the four options each use key phrases: movement of source, gap or obstacle, one plane, and sum of displacements.
Recall that diffraction is about what happens to wavefronts at an edge or narrow opening, not about frequency shift or filtering vibrations.
Compare the phrase about spreading through a gap or around an obstacle with the other three wave effects to pick the matching description.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the meaning of the term diffraction for a progressive transverse wave.
State the physical rule: diffraction is the spreading of waves into the shadow region when wavefronts pass a narrow gap or the edge of an obstacle.
Check option A: change in observed frequency due to source movement is the Doppler effect, so it does not match.
Check option C: oscillations confined to one plane is polarisation, possible only for transverse waves, so it does not match.
Check option D: resultant displacement equals the sum of individual displacements is the principle of superposition, so it does not match.
The remaining description of spreading through a gap or around an obstacle matches diffraction. This is option B.

A.explanation: This describes the Doppler effect, where motion of the source changes observed wavelength and frequency.

B.explanation: This is the definition of diffraction for any progressive wave meeting a gap or obstacle.

C.explanation: This describes polarisation, which confines transverse oscillations to one plane.

D.explanation: This describes the principle of superposition when two waves meet and combine.
